lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The QR responses took less time to submit and included two useful later reflections. I think the two-stage method worked.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I'm not completely convinced. What evidence supports the claim that the whole method worked?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Let’s separate the results. All three testers completed the paper form and marked an exact route location.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The average paper time was three minutes thirty-five seconds. Two testers skipped the open comment box.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: And the QR form?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Two testers completed it in about two minutes ten seconds. One stopped when the connection failed.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: The two completed QR responses added explanations that weren’t on paper. That suggests later reflection can add detail.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: It suggests that for those two responses, but it doesn’t show that a QR follow-up would work reliably for everyone.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Correct. The strongest evidence is about response type and prototype clarity, not visitor preference.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I can see the limitation. Still, the later comments described why two locations felt confusing.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I can see the case for an optional follow-up, but my concern is the failed connection and the tiny staff-only sample.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Are you saying the QR prototype has no value?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: No. I’m saying the evidence is narrower than your conclusion. One failure doesn’t prove the tool is unreliable, either.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Then what would change your mind about testing the optional stage again?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: A stable connection, clearer wording that paper is already complete, and testers who were not involved in planning the route.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That seems fair. Would five independent testers be enough to justify another internal check?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Enough to examine clarity and completion, perhaps. It still wouldn’t establish public preference.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So we seem to agree on the evidence: paper worked for all three; two QR responses added detail; one connection failed.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: And we still disagree about how much that supports a two-stage method.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Exactly. Let’s carry that precise disagreement into the final decision instead of forcing agreement now.
